examples.solution_text:
The smallest value with a dot is $2$ and the largest is $7$.
$\text{Range}=7-2=5$ books.
The tallest stack is above $4$, with four dots. The mode is $4$ books.

Team A: Each value occurs once. No value occurs more often than the others, so there is no mode.
Team B: $2$ and $4$ each occur three times, more often than any other value. The modes are $2$ and $4$ goals.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Stall A range}&=9-1\\&=8\text{ cups}\\\text{Stall B range}&=7-3\\&=4\text{ cups}\\\text{Difference}&=8-4\\&=4\text{ cups}\end{aligned}$
Stall A's range is $4$ cups greater. Stall B has more consistent sales because its range is smaller.
Stall A has modes $4$ and $6$ cups: both stacks have three dots. Stall B has mode $6$ cups: its tallest stack has four dots.
Both stalls include mode $6$, but Stall A also has mode $4$. Sharing a mode does not mean their ranges are equal.

examples.question_text:
Four groups recorded the number of points scored in games.
A: $12,18,15,20,14$
B: $8,11,22,16,9$
C: $14,14,15,16,16$
D: $17,17,17,17,17$
Calculate each range. Which group has the greatest spread? Which group has the most consistent scores? Also find Group D's mode.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{A range}&=20-12=8\\\text{B range}&=22-8=14\\\text{C range}&=16-14=2\\\text{D range}&=17-17=0\end{aligned}$
Group B has the greatest spread because its range is largest, $14$ points.
Group D has the most consistent scores because its range is $0$: all its scores are equal. Its mode is $17$ points, which occurs five times.

Used Stage 3 mathematics and different source values. Practice and quiz content were unchanged and were read only for method classification. Solution prose and mathematics inherit the renderer's blue; diagrams use black ink and explicit label sizes. Final-size visual verification remains for the capture stage.

examples.derivation: Observed endpoints are 2 and 7, giving range 7−2=5 books. Frequencies are 1, 2, 4, 2, 1 at values 2, 3, 4, 5, 7; the unique mode is 4 books.
Team A has one occurrence of each value 1–5, so it has no mode under the accepted convention. Team B has frequencies 1, 3, 1, 3, 1; both 2 and 4 goals are modes.

Stall A has range 9−1=8 cups and modes 4 and 6, each occurring three times. Stall B has range 7−3=4 cups and mode 6, occurring four times. The range difference is 8−4=4 cups. Stall B is more consistent; the shared mode does not imply equal ranges.
Ranges are A: 20−12=8, B: 22−8=14, C: 16−14=2, and D: 17−17=0 points. B has the greatest spread; D is most consistent. All five D values are 17, so its mode is 17 points.
